why: src/mcp-document-mutations.ts:277 resolves knowledge_base_name+path through kb-fs.ts resolveKbPath, which rejects absolute paths, '..' segments and null bytes, then realpath-checks every existing ancestor to confirm it stays inside the KB root before any write, and knowledge_base_name itself is confined to a single non-dotted, non-separator path.join child of the KB root via resolveKnowledgeBaseDir.

why: resolveIndexVersionPath (src/diff-index-core.ts:91-94) never runs the traversal/containment checks that kb-fs.ts applies to add_document/delete_document: an absolute `before`/`after` is returned untouched and a relative one is path.join'd onto modelDir with no rejection of '..' segments, so a caller can point diff_index at any directory on the host filesystem that happens to contain a faiss.index+docstore.json pair (e.g. a sibling model directory, a backup, or another tenant's index) and get back its document source paths, KB name and chunk identifiers via the similarity-search comparison. This is weakened to Tier B because the tool's own Zod schema/description explicitly documents 'BEFORE/AFTER index version number, relative directory, or absolute version directory' as an intended input shape (src/mcp-tool-specs.ts:122-123), so the absolute-path case is advertised behaviour rather than a pure oversight; the unrestricted relative-path traversal (no assertNoTraversal-style check at all, unlike every other path-handling helper in this repo) is the part that exceeds what a reasonable caller of a 'compare two persisted index versions' tool would expect, and I could not fully rule out that some real-world deployment host has such directories reachable from KB_INDEX_PATH.
contract: BEFORE index version number, relative directory, or absolute version directory.

excerpt: const targetPath = scriptPath || path.join(process.cwd(), `matlab_script_${Date.now()}.m`); fs.copyFileSync(tempFile, targetPath);
sink: fs.copyFileSync(tempFile, targetPath) writes the temp .m file (containing caller-supplied code) to an attacker-chosen absolute/relative path with no validation
why: scriptPath is a caller-controlled optional string per the tool's own inputSchema and is used verbatim as the destination of fs.copyFileSync with no path normalization, base-directory check, or extension/traversal restriction. A caller can pass e.g. an absolute path to overwrite any file the process user can write (config files, cron entries, startup scripts, other users' files), which is an integrity/availability impact beyond the tool's advertised purpose of merely 'executing MATLAB code'. This is distinct from the code-execution mechanism itself (which is the tool's stated purpose and not flagged here).
contract: Custom path to save the MATLAB script (optional)

excerpt: const targetPath = scriptPath || path.join(process.cwd(), `matlab_generated_${Date.now()}.m`); fs.writeFileSync(targetPath, generatedCode);
sink: fs.writeFileSync(targetPath, generatedCode) writes generated content (which itself embeds the caller's raw description string) to an attacker-chosen absolute/relative path with no validation
why: scriptPath is a caller-controlled optional string per the tool's own inputSchema and is passed unmodified as the destination path to fs.writeFileSync with no normalization, base-directory containment check, or path-traversal filtering. A caller supplying an absolute or ../-relative path can create or overwrite an arbitrary file on disk (the write also embeds the attacker's own 'description' text verbatim into the file, so content is also attacker-chosen), which is an integrity impact beyond generating a code snippet. generateCode() itself is a static template (no LLM call), so the only real sink here is the file write.
contract: Custom path to save the generated MATLAB script (optional)

why: jobId (validated as a UUID by the tool schema) is only used as a key into PipelineManager's in-memory jobMap to look up/cancel a job; it never reaches a path, command, SQL string, or eval.

sink: outbound HTTP(S) request to the caller-supplied URL's hostname (axios.get in HttpFetcher; Chromium's own network stack in BrowserFetcher's Playwright fallback)
guard: bypassable: ScraperAccessPolicy.assertNetworkUrlAllowed (src/utils/accessPolicy.ts:83-151) blocks private/special-use IPs, but it does this by resolving the hostname once via dns.promises.lookup at check time (accessPolicy.ts:83-151, called at HttpFetcher.ts:113 before the request); axios.get (line 161) then performs its own independent DNS resolution to actually connect, and nothing pins the checked address for that connection. An attacker who controls the authoritative DNS for the target hostname can answer the pre-check lookup with a public IP and the connect-time lookup, moments later, with a private/link-local address (e.g. 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254), defeating the check. The same applies to redirects: the Location header is revalidated (line 197) but the eventual connect to it is again a separate resolution.
why: url is directly caller-controlled per the tool's own zod schema (z.string().url()); it flows straight through AutoDetectFetcher into HttpFetcher, whose only SSRF defense is a check-then-connect hostname validation with no IP pinning between the two independent DNS resolutions. BrowserFetcher has the identical pattern (assertNetworkUrlAllowed before navigation, then Chromium resolves and connects on its own).
contract: Fetch a single URL and convert its content to Markdown. Use this tool to read the content of any web page.

why: library/targetVersion only feed a small bounded regex (/^(\d+)(?:\.(?:x(?:\.x)?|\d+(?:\.(?:x|\d+))?))?$|^$/, no nested quantifiers) and semver 7.8.5 (ReDoS fixes landed in 7.5.2) plus parameterized store lookups; no path/command/SQL sink is reached.
jobId is only used as a Map key in PipelineManager.getJob; it never reaches a path, command, SQL string, or eval.
status is a zod-validated enum used only to filter an in-memory job list; no caller-controlled string ever reaches a sink.
The tool takes no parameters at all (empty schema), so there is no caller-controlled input to trace.

library/version only feed the same bounded semver-coercion regex used by find_version (semver 7.8.5, ReDoS-patched) and parameterized store lookups; the eventual re-fetch reuses the version's already-stored, previously-validated sourceUrl rather than a fresh caller-supplied URL, so no new attacker-controlled string reaches the network/file sinks in this call.

library/version are only used in parameterized DocumentStore delete statements (db.prepare(...).run with ? placeholders) and an in-memory job-list filter by equality; no string concatenation into SQL/paths/commands occurs.

sink: new RegExp(userPattern) compiled from a caller-supplied string, then .test() run once per discovered URL/pathname/basename for every page visited during the crawl (src/scraper/strategies/BaseScraperStrategy.ts:144 shouldIncludeUrl -> patternMatcher.ts matchesAnyPattern/patternToRegExp)
why: The tool's own schema documents that '/pattern/' is treated as a literal regex the caller supplies, and PipelineManager.normalizeScraperOptions spreads options unchanged so includePatterns/excludePatterns reach patternToRegExp verbatim with no length/complexity limit or timeout. Because scrape_docs's url argument is also caller-controlled, an attacker can point it at their own site and pick both a catastrophic-backtracking pattern and page content/links engineered to hit it, hanging the scrape (and the shared worker) for the whole crawl (up to maxPages). Note: scrape_docs's url also goes through the same DNS-rebinding-bypassable SSRF check documented under fetch_url; that finding applies here too but only one row is filed per tool.
contract: Patterns for including/excluding URLs during scraping... Regex patterns must be wrapped in slashes, e.g. /pattern/.

why: DocumentStore.escapeFtsQuery (DocumentStore.ts:882) tokenizes the caller-supplied query with a quote-toggle state machine and doubles every embedded quote before building the FTS5 MATCH string, and library/version resolve through parameterized statements, preventing FTS5 query-syntax injection.

sink: fetch() to JungleBus API with caller string spliced unescaped into the URL path
why: txid is an optional free-form string (no format check, unlike bsv_decodeTransaction's isTxid regex) concatenated raw into the path. A value containing '/' and '..' segments (e.g. '../../v1/other') is normalized by the URL/fetch parser and can replace the entire '/transaction/get/' prefix, letting the caller redirect the request to any other path on the fixed junglebusUrl() host with no validation at all. Impact is capped because the host is fixed (server-configured) and no secret headers are attached on this call, so I flag Tier B rather than A.

sink: witApi.queryByWiql({ query }, teamContext) -- query is a WIQL string built by direct template interpolation of caller-controlled projectId/teamId into a single-quoted WIQL string literal
why: projectId and teamId are plain optional z.string() fields in ListWorkItemsSchema (schemas.ts) with no quote-escaping or allow-list. When the caller omits `wiql`, constructDefaultWiql() builds the query by directly interpolating projectId/teamId inside single-quoted WIQL literals with zero escaping, then passes it straight to witApi.queryByWiql(). A projectId such as `x' OR ''='` breaks out of the intended `[System.TeamProject] = '<value>'` filter and turns the WHERE clause into a tautology, returning work items across every project the caller's credentials can see instead of the single project the tool call declared -- i.e. the caller-supplied scoping parameter can be used to defeat the query's own scoping, structurally identical to a classic SQL injection via string concatenation. I traced every hop: schema -> index.ts dispatch (passes args.projectId unmodified when provided) -> constructDefaultWiql -> witApi.queryByWiql. The sink is this repo's own string-building code, not the azure-devops-node-api library (which faithfully executes whatever WIQL text it is given), so no dependency check was needed.

excerpt: const client = await azureDevOpsClient.getWikiClient({ organizationId, projectId });
sink: WikiClient constructor (src/clients/azure-devops.ts) calls resolveAzureDevOpsBaseUrls(organizationUrl, { organizationId, ... }); inside that helper (src/shared/azure-devops-url.ts:33) `options.organizationId ?? extractServicesOrganization(url)` lets the caller-supplied organizationId override the org segment extracted from the deployment's configured AZURE_DEVOPS_ORG_URL, so every subsequent WikiClient HTTP call (getPage) is sent to https://dev.azure.com/<caller-supplied-org>/... using the deployment's own PAT/Bearer credential.
why: organizationId is a plain optional z.string() in GetWikiPageSchema with no allow-list against the configured org. Traced schema -> wikis/index.ts (passes args.organizationId ?? defaultOrg, i.e. caller value wins when supplied) -> getWikiPage -> azureDevOpsClient.getWikiClient({organizationId}) -> WikiClient constructor -> resolveAzureDevOpsBaseUrls, which prefers options.organizationId over the org parsed from the real configured URL whenever the hostname is dev.azure.com/*.visualstudio.com. This lets a caller (or a prompt-injected agent acting on this tool) redirect wiki reads to any other Azure DevOps organization the deployment's PAT/identity token can reach, beyond the single org the operator intended to expose via AZURE_DEVOPS_ORG_URL. Marked Tier B rather than A because real-world impact depends on whether the configured credential actually has access to more than one org (cannot confirm statically), and the destination host itself is not attacker-arbitrary (always dev.azure.com/*.visualstudio.com), which caps it below a full SSRF.

A caller can create/overwrite a wiki page in an org other than the one the deployment operator intended, using the deployment's own credential. Tier B for the same reason as get_wiki_page: requires the configured PAT/identity to actually span multiple orgs, which cannot be confirmed statically, and the destination host is still restricted to dev.azure.com/*.visualstudio.com.

why: Unlike the other five wiki tools, get_wikis does not go through the hand-rolled WikiClient at all -- it calls connection.getWikiApi().getAllWikis(projectId) on the fixed, server-startup-configured WebApi connection. The organizationId field in GetWikisSchema is accepted by zod but is never read by the getWikis() feature function, so it is a dead parameter with no effect (confirmed by reading src/features/wikis/get-wikis/feature.ts, which destructures only { projectId } from options).

sink: resolveAzureDevOpsBaseUrls(connection.serverUrl, { organizationId: options.organizationId, projectId }) lets caller-supplied organizationId override the org segment of searchBaseUrl (same mechanism as the wiki tools); projectId is then concatenated raw (no encodeURIComponent) into the axios.post URL path, so a value containing '/' or '../' alters which path segment ends up before the fixed '_apis/search/codesearchresults' suffix.
why: SearchCodeOptions.organizationId/projectId are plain strings from SearchCodeSchema with no validation. Traced schema -> index.ts -> searchCode() -> resolveAzureDevOpsBaseUrls (org override, same bug class as wikis) -> raw template-literal URL with unescaped projectId -> axios.post carrying the deployment's PAT/Bearer Authorization header. A caller can redirect the authenticated code-search request to a different org and/or manipulate the project segment of the path (e.g. via '../' sequences, which the WHATWG URL normalizer collapses when axios/Node parses the final URL) to reach a different project's or org's search scope than the one the tool call declared, using the deployment's own credential. The fixed '_apis/search/codesearchresults' suffix limits this to the search API surface rather than arbitrary endpoints, which is why this is Tier B, not A: real exposure depends on the credential's actual multi-org/multi-project reach, which is not confirmable from static code.

sink: caller string is embedded verbatim (only wrapped with `(?i).*` / `.*`) into a regex string, bound as the Cypher $query parameter, and evaluated server-side via `e.name =~ $query OR e.entityType =~ $query OR e.observations =~ $query` (line 481) against every Entity node's name/entityType/observations
why: Traced callToolHandler.ts:83-91 (`knowledgeGraphManager.searchNodes(args.query)`) -> KnowledgeGraphManager.searchNodes (delegates straight to storageProvider since a Neo4j StorageProvider is present) -> Neo4jStorageProvider.searchNodes, which builds the regex string by naive template interpolation and runs it through Neo4j's `=~` operator, which uses Java's backtracking regex engine. listToolsHandler.ts declares `query` as an opaque free-text string ('match against entity names, types, and observation content'), giving no indication to the caller that it is regex syntax, and there is no length cap, metacharacter escaping, or execution timeout anywhere on this path. An adversarial value such as query=`(a+)+$` yields the compiled pattern `(?i).*(a+)+$.*`, which triggers catastrophic backtracking against long observation/entityType strings already stored in the graph (attacker can also first store such a string via add_observations), tying up the Neo4j query thread and, by extension, the MCP server's single request-processing path. Checked node_modules/neo4j-driver 5.28.1: session.run()/executeQuery() only serializes and transmits parameters over Bolt, performing no regex validation or sanitization; the regex is actually evaluated inside the external Neo4j DBMS process, which is not a vendored dependency of this repo.

sink: Values are substituted with Python str.format_map directly inside single-quoted SQL string literals in a WHERE clause, then the resulting SQL text is executed via handle_base_readQuery -> conn.execute(text(sql)) with no escaping.
why: app.py's create_custom_query_handler (lines 812-831) detects '{' in the YAML sql template and calls sql.format_map(kwargs) before execution; table_name/database_name are declared plain str parameters with no format constraints. Because the substitution lands inside existing single quotes ('...{table_name}...'), a value containing a single quote breaks out of the literal (e.g. table_name = "x' UNION SELECT username,password,1,1,1 FROM DBC.LogonRules WHERE '1'='1") and is appended verbatim to a real SELECT statement executed via base_tools.handle_base_readQuery's conn.execute(text(sql)) (base_tools.py line 71-82), which has no additional sanitization. sink: setByPath (called from ScratchpadManager.jsonSet/jsonInsert in src/server/scratchpad/manager.ts on the JSON.parse()'d scratchpad buffer) writes params.value to a property resolved by walking the caller-supplied path segments with no denylist for '__proto__', 'constructor' or 'prototype'.
why: operation:'json_set' (or json_insert/json_delete) with path:'$.__proto__.<key>' on a format:'json' scratchpad reaches setByPath in src/server/scratchpad/json-path.ts. Because the intermediate object has no OWN '__proto__' data property (a fresh {} buffer), the bracket-access `current[String(segments[i])]` in the traversal loop (line 47) returns the object's real inherited [[Prototype]] (Object.prototype itself) rather than a plain data field, and the final assignment on line 54 then writes the caller's value directly onto Object.prototype. I extracted the exact parsePath/setByPath logic (verbatim from json-path.ts) into an isolated Node script (not the target repo) and confirmed Object.prototype.polluted becomes 'gotcha' process-wide after one json_set call, invisible in the tool's own JSON.stringify output since it's not an own property. Neither json-path.ts nor manager.ts contains any '__proto__'/'constructor'/'prototype' filtering (verified by grep). Impact is global to the running MCP server process (integrity of every plain object thereafter, including safety/config checks that read possibly-undefined properties), not merely a crash. The precise CWE is CWE-1321 (Prototype Pollution), which is not in the given taxonomy; CWE-915 (Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes) is the closest listed analog.

guard: partial: verifyPathSafety(filePath) resolves fs.realpath(filePath) and rejects anything outside the workspace, but only when the target path already exists; if the final component does not exist yet, fs.realpath throws ENOENT and the function returns success unchecked (workspace.ts:190-193), so a write/mkdir/compress/decompress to 'existingSymlinkedDir/newfile' never has its parent-directory symlink validated.
why: Traced resolveWorkspacePath -> verifyPathSafety -> fs.mkdir(dirname, {recursive:true}) -> fs.writeFile in the 'write' case of src/server/handlers/workspace.ts: if a directory inside the workspace were already a symlink to an external path, writing a NEW file under it would skip the realpath check (ENOENT on the not-yet-existing full path) and fs.writeFile would then follow the symlink outside the sandbox. I could not find any operation exposed by manage_workspace, or by any other tool in this shard, that creates a symlink inside the workspace (move/mkdir/compress/decompress only rename or write regular files/directories), so I cannot confirm the precondition (a pre-existing symlink placed there by something other than this tool) is reachable purely through caller-controlled arguments — hence Tier B rather than A.

'saveTo' (the only local-filesystem write this tool does) goes through resolveLocalMediaPath, which confines it to MEDIA_LOCAL_FILE_ROOT (path.relative()-based containment check) when set, and refuses local paths entirely over the HTTP transport when MEDIA_LOCAL_FILE_ROOT is unset -- verified in src/tools/powershell/media/local-files.ts and media-download.ts. 'command'/'category'/'search' are matched against an in-memory index built once from a fixed, vendored directory list (DOCUMENTATION_CATEGORIES); findCommand() does a case-insensitive equality match against doc.name in that index and only then reads doc.file, a path the index itself computed -- no caller string is ever concatenated into a filesystem path (src/tools/powershell/documentation-index.ts).

excerpt: addresses = await lookup(url.hostname, { all: true }); ... const blocked = addresses.filter(...)
sink: server-side fetch() of a caller-supplied URL, after a one-time DNS-based private-IP check
guard: bypassable: DNS-rebinding -- attacker's nameserver returns a public IP for the check-time lookup() and a private/link-local IP for the later fetch()-time resolution
why: sourceUrl is fetched by the server itself. assertFetchableSourceUrl (src/tools/powershell/media/local-files.ts) blocks private/loopback/link-local addresses by calling dns.lookup() on the hostname and rejecting if any resolved address is private -- a real allow-list. But the actual request is then made with Node's global fetch() (utils.ts fetchWithTimeout), which performs its OWN independent DNS resolution at connect time. Because the check and the connect are two separate DNS lookups, an attacker who controls authoritative DNS for the sourceUrl hostname can answer the first lookup (the check) with a public IP and the second lookup (the actual fetch/connect, moments later) with 169.254.169.254 or another RFC1918 address -- classic DNS-rebinding TOCTOU. The per-redirect re-validation in fetchSourceUrl closes the redirect-based bypass but does nothing for this one, since it re-runs the same check-then-fetch pattern. Concrete bypass: host a domain whose authoritative nameserver returns 93.184.216.34 (public) on the first A query and 169.254.169.254 on the second/subsequent A query (TTL=0/1), then pass http://that-domain/ as sourceUrl.
contract: Source is exactly one of sourceUrl (fetched by this server -- use this to import from a live site), filePath ..., or content (base64).

sink: unescaped path segment in an Item Service REST GET URL (RestfulItemServiceClient.getItemById)
why: 'id' is a plain z.string() with no GUID/format restriction, and is concatenated unescaped directly into the Item Service REST URL path (getItemById, src/tools/item-service/client.ts line 149), unlike the sibling getItemByPath()/createItem() methods in the same file which correctly wrap their path input in encodeURIComponent (lines 243 and 286). Node's fetch() constructs a WHATWG URL from this string, which performs RFC-3986 dot-segment normalization on the path component: a value such as '../../users' collapses one or more '/sitecore/api/ssc/item/' segments away and can redirect the authenticated request (same session cookie) to a different path under the same Item Service host -- reaching an endpoint this tool's own declared 'by ID' contract does not intend to expose, and potentially bypassing any path-scoped access control (e.g. a reverse proxy/WAF rule) that assumes traffic only ever hits /item/<opaque-id>. Impact beyond that (which other same-host endpoints exist and what they expose) depends on the specific Sitecore/Item-Service deployment, which cannot be confirmed from this repo alone.

Node's fetch() constructs a WHATWG URL from this string, which performs RFC-3986 dot-segment normalization on the path component: a value such as '../../users' collapses one or more '/sitecore/api/ssc/item/' segments away and can redirect the authenticated request (same session cookie) to a different path under the same Item Service host -- reaching an endpoint this tool's own declared 'by ID' contract does not intend to expose, and potentially bypassing any path-scoped access control (e.g. a reverse proxy/WAF rule) that assumes traffic only ever hits /item/<opaque-id>. Impact beyond that (which other same-host endpoints exist and what they expose) depends on the specific Sitecore/Item-Service deployment, which cannot be confirmed from this repo alone.
contract: Get the direct children of a Sitecore item by its ID, with all their fields.

excerpt: const children = await client.getItemChildren(idToProcess, options) as any;
sink: root 'id' flows unescaped into the same getItemChildren() REST GET URL as item-service-get-item-children
why: This tool's caller-supplied root 'id' (src/tools/item-service/logic/composite/get-item-descendants.ts) is passed straight into RestfulItemServiceClient.getItemChildren, which concatenates it unescaped into the REST URL path (client.ts line 195) -- the same missing-encodeURIComponent gap as item-service-get-item-children. Only the root id is caller-controlled; subsequent queue entries come from Sitecore's own ItemID field values, so the injection surface is limited to the first request of the traversal.
contract: Gets every descendant of a Sitecore item by ID, with all their fields.

param: GRAPHQL_HEADERS (server config, reflected verbatim in the tool's own output)
sink: server config value returned unmasked in the 'config' tool's CallToolResult / config://main resource
guard: partial: redactConfig masks every credential field it enumerates (apiKey, both passwords, authoring token/secret, authorizationHeader) but omits graphQL.headers, an operator-supplied arbitrary header map that is exactly where a custom secret header would live
why: redactConfig() (src/config.ts, ~line 229) masks graphQL.apiKey, itemService.password, powershell.password, authoring.token, authoring.clientSecret and authorizationHeader before the 'config' tool/'config://main' resource return the config -- but it does not mask 'graphQL.headers', a caller-configurable map populated from the GRAPHQL_HEADERS env var (parseGraphQLHeaders, config.ts line 143) that operators use for exactly the kind of value redactConfig otherwise exists to hide -- a custom Authorization/X-Api-Key header for a gateway in front of the GraphQL Edge endpoint. If an operator sets such a header, its value is returned verbatim by this read-only tool to anyone who can call it, which over TRANSPORT=streamable-http (AUTHORIZATION_HEADER empty by default per this repo's own AGENTS.md) is anyone who can reach the port. This depends on whether an operator actually put a secret in GRAPHQL_HEADERS, which cannot be confirmed statically.
contract: Prints the configuration of the Sitecore MCP server. Secrets (passwords, the GraphQL API key, the authorization header) are redacted.

why: run_accounting_health_across in tools_cross_instance.py only fans out read-only fetch_aging_lines/search_read calls across instances resolved via select_instances(), which is bounded to the operator-configured instance allowlist (cross_instance.py select_instances/parse_instances_meta); no caller-controlled host/URL escapes that list.

tools_accounting.py's accounting_health_summary takes only an optional instance name (validated against configured instances) and forwards to build_unreconciled_summary, which issues read-only search_count/search_read calls; no caller-controlled sink beyond the caller's own Odoo account.

run_aggregate_across (tools_cross_instance.py) validates model via validate_model_name, parses measures via parse_measure_spec's fixed aggregator allowlist, applies field_policy.check_aggregate per instance, and only queries instances from the configured allowlist via select_instances; the read_group call is forwarded to the caller's own Odoo instance.

tools_read.py's aggregate_records validates the model name, parses each measure through parse_measure_spec's fixed aggregator allowlist, blocks denied fields via field_policy.check_aggregate, and forwards group_by/domain/measures to the caller's own Odoo server via odoo.execute_method(read_group/formatted_read_group); domain itself is normalized through normalize_domain_input which uses ast.literal_eval/json.loads, never eval, so there is no local injection surface.

analyze_upgrade_log_report (diagnostics.py) only takes log_text as a string, truncates it to MAX_LOG_BYTES, and regex-matches each line against a fixed, bounded pattern list (patterns use small {0,80} quantifiers); it never opens a file path, never contacts Odoo, and never executes anything derived from the text.

build_domain_report (agent_tools.py) only validates conditions against SAFE_DOMAIN_OPERATORS and optional fields_metadata and returns the constructed domain list; it never executes the domain against Odoo or anywhere else.

business_pack_report (tools_diagnostics.py) uses the caller-supplied 'pack' string only to select a static bucket in build_business_pack_report; when use_live_metadata is true it only calls read-only odoo.get_models()/get_installed_modules(), never a write or arbitrary method.

cancel_async_task only cancels a pending/running entry in the process-wide AsyncTaskManager by task_id (task_queue.py); this server's design gives every caller the same underlying Odoo service-account identity per instance (credentials are configured server-side per instance, not per MCP caller), so there is no distinct principal being denied authorization here any more than the bare-stdio/no-transport-auth property the task explicitly excludes from per-tool findings; task_id is a 48-bit uuid4 hex, not sequential.

sink: odoo.execute_method(model, "message_post", [record_id], **canonical["kwargs"]) — executes immediately once the supplied approval.token string-matches a value computed purely from the caller's own request fields
guard: bypassable: token is odoo-write:sha256(canonical_json(payload))[:32] (agent_tools.build_approval_token) with no server secret and no session-side registration (unlike preview_write/validate_write, chatter_post never calls register_write_approval/require_validated_write_approval). A caller can compute the identical hash from the exact model/record_id/body/message_type/subtype_xmlid/partner_ids/attachment_ids/instance it is about to send and pass approval={'token': <that hash>}, confirm=true on the very first call, fully skipping the 'preview first' step the tool's own description promises ('Default mode requires an approval token returned from a preview call').
why: The tool's declared safety contract is a two-step preview-then-confirm gate for a DESTRUCTIVE_TOOL, but the 'approval' is only a deterministic hash of caller-controlled fields with no secret or server-side state, so it authorizes nothing beyond what the caller already asserted about its own request. This is a real, concretely-demonstrated bypass of the tool's own stated authorization gate, contrasted directly with the properly session-registered gate used by preview_write/validate_write/execute_approved_write in the same file.
contract: Default mode requires an approval token returned from a preview call; set MCP_CHATTER_DIRECT=1 to bypass and post immediately.

why: data_quality_report (tools_data_quality.py) validates model name, clamps sample_limit, and delegates to build_data_quality_report which only issues search_read/search_count/execute_method('search',...) read-only calls; relation 'target' models for the orphan check come from Odoo's own fields_get metadata (meta['relation']), not caller input.

diagnose_access (tools_diagnostics.py) explicitly documents and implements read-only metadata/count calls only (search_read on ir.model, context_get, search_count) with no sudo/impersonation; domain/record_ids are normalized the same safe way as search_records and forwarded to the caller's own Odoo account.

diagnose_odoo_call_report (diagnostics.py) is a pure input-driven classifier over model/method/args/kwargs/metadata; it never calls odoo.execute_method or any network/file API, matching its 'without executing it' description which we verified in the code rather than trusting the docstring alone.

_execute_approved_write_gated (tools_write.py) requires verify_write_approval to match, then require_validated_write_approval(app_context, approval) to find a non-expired record that was only created by a prior validate_write call in this same server session (server_core.register_write_approval/require_validated_write_approval, TTL-bound), then re-checks write_approval_payload equality, confirm=true, and writes_enabled(); a caller cannot forge entry into app_context.write_approvals merely by computing the token hash, unlike chatter_post.

excerpt: if method in READ_ONLY_METHODS or method.startswith(("get_", "_get_")):
sink: odoo.execute_method(model, method, *args, **kwargs) in tools_write.py execute_method — runs whatever method name passed classify_method_safety with caller-supplied args/kwargs
guard: partial: classify_method_safety() (diagnostics.py) is a pure name-based heuristic; DESTRUCTIVE_METHODS (create/write/unlink) are hard-blocked and SIDE_EFFECT_METHOD_PATTERNS/'unknown' methods require an explicit allowlist entry or ODOO_MCP_ALLOW_UNKNOWN_METHODS, but any existing Odoo/addon method merely named starting with 'get_' or '_get_' is classified 'read_only' (even at only medium confidence) and is exempt from that review gate entirely.
why: If the connected Odoo instance has any custom method (a real possibility in third-party addons, which are not part of this repo) named with a get_/_get_ prefix that nonetheless performs a write or side effect, execute_method will run it with caller-supplied args/kwargs without ever requiring policy-file/env allowlisting, purely because of the name heuristic. We could not confirm from this repo's own code whether such a method exists on any real target instance, so this stays Tier B rather than A.
contract: Odoo model method to call; direct create, write, and unlink are blocked.

why: build_fit_gap_report (diagnostics.py) only classifies caller-supplied requirements/available_models/available_fields/installed_modules into static buckets; it never contacts Odoo or any other sink even when use_live_metadata is set (the tool only appends an info-level note, it does not fetch anything).

generate_json2_payload_report (diagnostics.py) only string-formats an endpoint path/URL and JSON body preview; it never issues an HTTP request (confirmed by reading the function body, which does no urllib/requests call), matching the 'without network access' description.

get_async_task only polls AsyncTaskManager.status(task_id) in the process-wide task store; as with cancel_async_task, every caller of this server shares the same underlying Odoo service-account identity per configured instance, so there is no distinct-privilege boundary being crossed by reading another call's task result within one process, and task_id (uuid4 hex[:12]) is not guessable/sequential.

get_model_fields validates the model name, forwards to odoo.get_model_fields (a read-only fields_get), applies field_policy redaction markers, and only reorders/filters the returned dict locally; no execution or injection surface.

get_odoo_profile returns url/hostname/db/username/transport/verify_ssl/server_version/user_context/installed_modules — no password or API key field is ever included (confirmed by reading the exact dict built in tools_read.py), so there is no credential exposure, and the rest is a read-only forward to the caller's own instance.
health_check takes no arguments and only reports locally computed posture (surface counts, rate_report(), plugin_posture(), runtime_security_report()); there is no caller-controlled input to trace.

index_knowledge validates the model name, normalizes domain safely, fetches via read-only odoo.search_read, applies field_policy.redact_records before indexing, and stores documents purely in an in-process BM25 dict (knowledge_index.py) — there is no filesystem path derived from caller input anywhere in this path.
inspect_model_relationships_report only reads/uses fields_get-shaped metadata (caller-supplied or fetched read-only) to compute relationship/required-field summaries; no write or execution path.
knowledge_stats takes no arguments and only returns get_knowledge_store().stats(), a local in-memory summary of index sizes.

list_async_tasks takes no caller-controlled arguments and returns only name/status/timestamps for tasks (never the result payload, per TaskRecord.snapshot(include_result=False)); no sensitive data or sink is reachable through this tool.

list_instances takes no arguments and list_configured_instances() (odoo_client.py) builds its summary from an explicit key allowlist (url/db/transport/is_default/tags/cross_instance) that never copies username/password, so there is no credential exposure and no caller-controlled input to trace.

list_models forwards to read-only odoo.get_models() and filters the returned list locally in Python using a caller-supplied substring query; the substring is never sent back to Odoo as part of a domain, so there is no injection surface.

lookup_model_history_report (agent_tools.py) only looks the caller-supplied name string up in a static, curated rename/removal catalog baked into the source; it never contacts Odoo or executes anything, matching its 'static and never contacts Odoo' description which we verified in the code.

preview_write only builds a canonical approval-token report via build_write_preview_report; it validates model name and operation shape but never calls odoo.execute_method or otherwise mutates Odoo state — actual execution only happens later through execute_approved_write's separate, session-gated path.

read_attachment only takes an integer attachment_id (validated > 0) and reads ir.attachment fields/datas via odoo.execute_method('ir.attachment','read',...) against the caller's own Odoo server — it never opens a local filesystem path, so there is no path-traversal surface despite the name suggesting file access.

read_record validates model name and record_id>0, resolves a safe field list via resolve_read_fields, and forwards to odoo.read_records — a straightforward read-only ORM call to the caller's own instance, with field_policy redaction applied on the result.

receivable_payable_aging validates direction against a fixed 2-value set, clamps limit/top_partners, and delegates to build_direction_aging/fetch_aging_lines which only issue read-only search_read calls against account.move.line on the caller's own instance.

scan_addons_source passes addons_paths through restrict_addons_paths (server_core.py), which resolves each candidate path (Path.resolve, following symlinks and normalizing '..') and rejects any path not equal to or contained within an operator-configured ODOO_ADDONS_PATHS root, raising if no roots are configured at all; the scan loop itself also skips symlinked files. This closes the traversal path a caller-supplied addons_paths could otherwise attempt (e.g. '../../etc').

schema_catalog validates model names, caches by a JSON key of its own inputs, and only calls read-only odoo.get_models()/get_model_fields(); caller-controlled 'query' is only used for a local substring filter, never forwarded as an Odoo domain.

run_search_across validates model name, normalizes domain safely, and resolves the 'instances' selector through select_instances() which is bounded to the operator's configured instance list (cross_instance.py); each worker's search_read is a read-only call to that caller-selected-but-allowlisted instance.

search_employee forwards the caller's 'name' string as the 'name' kwarg of Odoo's own hr.employee.name_search method via odoo.execute_method — a fixed method/model with no locally-interpreted injection surface; the search semantics are entirely Odoo server-side.

search_holidays validates start_date/end_date with strptime (rejecting non-YYYY-MM-DD input), builds a domain list of Odoo [field, operator, value] leaves (values are plain strings/ints passed as domain terms, not concatenated into any query string), and forwards to read-only odoo.search_read.

search_knowledge validates the model name and only queries the local in-process BM25 KnowledgeStore.search(); it 'never contacts Odoo' (verified in code — no odoo client is even resolved in this tool), and the query string is only tokenized locally, never interpreted as code or a path.

search_records validates model name, normalizes domain via normalize_domain_input (json.loads/ast.literal_eval, never eval, with strict shape validation rejecting anything it can't fully parse), clamps limit, and forwards to read-only odoo.search_read on the caller's own instance, with field_policy redaction applied to results.

submit_async_task dispatches on the caller-supplied 'operation' string through a closed if/elif chain against fixed literals (never getattr/eval/dynamic lookup) in tools_async.py; each branch builds its job through the same validated per-tool helpers (restrict_addons_paths, validate_model_name, normalize_domain_input) already reviewed as clear/guarded for their synchronous counterparts, and writes are explicitly never accepted here.

build_upgrade_risk_report (diagnostics.py) only classifies caller-supplied module/method/source_findings/observed_errors data against static rule tables; it is input-driven and never calls odoo.execute_method even when use_live_metadata is set (that flag only appends an informational note), matching the 'without executing Odoo calls' description which we verified in the code.

validate_write only reads live model metadata via odoo.get_model_fields (read-only) and, when that succeeds, registers a server-side approval record (register_write_approval); it never itself calls create/write/unlink — actual execution requires the separately-gated execute_approved_write path.

The `operation` string is only used as a lookup key into the in-memory operation registry (getOperation/isOperationAllowed in src/operations/registry.ts and access.ts) to return that operation's schema/example metadata; it never reaches a filesystem, network, shell, or eval sink.

Every enabled read operation (search_pages, get_page, get_page_markdown, query_database, get_block_children, list_file_uploads, get_file_upload, get_file_url, get_image, etc., across src/operations/*.ts) resolves caller ids/filters into JSON bodies sent to api.notion.com via the official @notionhq/client SDK (src/services/notion.ts); the two places that touch a URL directly, get_file_url and get_image in src/operations/files.ts, only ever resolve and fetch a Notion-minted signed URL for an object Notion hosts (URL_LIKE guard rejects a caller-supplied URL outright, and hosted/https checks gate the actual fetch), so there is no injection, path, or SSRF surface a caller controls.

sink: node:fs/promises readFile() on a caller-supplied absolute or ~-relative filesystem path, with the resulting bytes uploaded to Notion's file_uploads API and optionally attached to a page/block the caller names
guard: partial: resolveUploadPath() (src/operations/files.ts lines 95-111) only confines the path to NOTION_UPLOAD_ROOT when that env var is set; when it is unset -- the documented default ("Unset means no confinement, which is the behavior before this existed") -- expandHome() is applied and the raw path is read with no restriction at all
why: The `source.path` field is genuinely caller-controlled per upload_file's own zod schema and description ("Local filesystem path (absolute, or ~-relative)"), and every hop -- schema parse in dispatch/index.ts -> upload_file handler -> resolveUploadPath -> readFile -- was read. With NOTION_UPLOAD_ROOT unset (the out-of-the-box state), any caller able to invoke notion_write can read an arbitrary file the server process can read (SSH keys, .env, /etc/passwd, source) and exfiltrate its bytes by uploading it to Notion and attaching it to a page the caller can view -- a genuine confidentiality violation that exceeds the tool's advertised Notion-access contract, not mere robustness or a crash.
contract: Local path: `source: { type: "path", path: "/abs/or/~/file.pdf" }` (server reads the file directly -- preferred for local files; filename is derived from the path if omitted).

why: The only value sent to the addon's set_telemetry_consent sink is a hardcoded False; user_prompt is never used as an argument to any sink.

asset_id/asset_type/resolution/file_format only build a request URL to the trusted api.polyhaven.com and select a dict key; the one caller-adjacent file-write path (extra 'include' files for glTF models, addon.py ~1700) is protected by an effective absolute-path/'..'/prefix check before any file is written to disk.

model_id is URL-quoted before use in the API path and is separately sanitized with re.sub to [A-Za-z0-9_-] before being used as a filename component (addon.py download_polypizza_model); only a single .glb is written, no archive extraction occurs.

uid only selects which Sketchfab-hosted model zip is fetched via the official API; before extractall, addon.py checks every zip member's normalized absolute path against the temp dir prefix and explicitly rejects any '..' segment, so path traversal in the downloaded archive is blocked.

Arbitrary Python execution inside Blender is this tool's entire declared purpose (docstring: 'Execute arbitrary Python code in Blender'), so bare execution is not itself a finding under the advertised-purpose rule. An opt-in AST allowlist (safe_mode.py, gated by BLENDER_MCP_SAFE_MODE, off by default) further restricts scripts when enabled. I reviewed its dunder/attribute blocklist, the getattr/setattr literal-name requirement, the unrooted-navigation backstop for unresolvable receivers, and the module-value-use anti-laundering check (blocking `x = bpy.ops; x.wm.append(...)`), and found no bypass reaching eval/exec/open/os/subprocess or the blocked bpy.ops.script/handlers/timers/registration surface.

sink: reads raw bytes of any local file path via open(path,'rb'); server.py then base64-encodes the bytes and forwards them as 'images' to the addon's create_rodin_job command, which (MAIN_SITE mode, addon.py create_rodin_job_main_site) multipart-uploads the decoded bytes to the third-party Rodin API at https://hyperhuman.deemos.com/api/v2/rodin
why: input_image_paths is declared as 'The absolute paths of input images' but the code's only check is os.path.exists(i) -- existence, not that the path is inside any expected directory or actually an image. Every path supplied is opened, read in full, base64-encoded, and uploaded to an external third-party service (Rodin/hyperhuman.deemos.com) using the user's own API key. A caller (or a model steered by prompt injection -- exactly the threat model safe_mode.py's own docstring names: 'third-party text ... could steer the model into writing hostile code') can pass e.g. ~/.ssh/id_rsa or any config file readable by the Blender process and have its contents exfiltrated off-box. This exceeds the advertised 'input image' contract and has no guard beyond existence-checking.
contract: input_image_paths: The **absolute** paths of input images. Even if only one image is provided, wrap it into a list.

sink: when input_image_url does not match ^https?://, addon.py's create_hunyuan_job_main_site (OFFICIAL_API mode) opens it as a local file path with open(image,'rb'), base64-encodes it, and POSTs it as ImageBase64 to Tencent Cloud's ai3d SubmitHunyuanTo3DProJob API; create_hunyuan_job_local_site (LOCAL_API mode, addon.py:3499) does the same and posts to a configured local /generate endpoint
why: server.py forwards input_image_url unchanged as 'image' to the addon's create_hunyuan_job command. The only branching logic in addon.py is a regex test for an http(s) scheme; anything else is treated as a local filesystem path with no directory confinement, extension check, or content validation, then its raw bytes are read and shipped to a third-party cloud API (or a local endpoint). Same exfiltration mechanism and same lack of guard as generate_hyper3d_model_via_images's input_image_paths.
contract: input_image_url: (Optional) The local or remote url of the input image. Accepts None if only using text prompt.

why: text_prompt and the numerically-validated bbox_condition (via _process_bbox, which rejects non-positive values) are only forwarded as form/JSON fields to Rodin's own API (hyperhuman.deemos.com or fal.run) using the caller's own configured API key; no path, command, or query surface.
user_prompt is the only caller-supplied value and it is only used as elicitation-prompt/telemetry context text; it never reaches a file, command, URL-path, or query sink.
No caller-controlled arguments beyond user_prompt (unused as a sink); the tool only forwards a fixed get_hunyuan3d_status command to the addon, which reports enabled/disabled state.
No caller-controlled arguments beyond user_prompt (unused as a sink); the tool only forwards a fixed get_hyper3d_status command to the addon.
object_name is only used as a lookup key in bpy.data.objects.get(name); the result is read-only scene introspection (location/rotation/scale/materials/mesh stats), no file, command, or network sink.

asset_type is validated against a fixed allowlist (['hdris','textures','models','all']) in addon.py get_polyhaven_categories before being interpolated into the api.polyhaven.com request path; invalid values are rejected before the request is made.
No caller-controlled arguments beyond user_prompt (unused as a sink); only forwards a fixed get_polyhaven_status command to the addon.
No caller-controlled arguments beyond user_prompt (unused as a sink); only forwards a fixed get_polypizza_status command to the addon.
No caller-controlled arguments beyond the required user_prompt (unused as a sink); returns read-only scene/object summary data from bpy.context.scene.

uid selects which Sketchfab-hosted model's info/thumbnail is fetched via the official api.sketchfab.com endpoints using the caller's own API key; the thumbnail URL itself comes from Sketchfab's own API response, not the caller, and the destination host is fixed.
No caller-controlled arguments beyond user_prompt (unused as a sink); only forwards a fixed get_sketchfab_status command to the addon.

The screenshot filepath is built server-side from tempfile.gettempdir() and os.getpid() only; max_size (caller-controlled int) is passed through to Blender's own screenshot-resize logic with no path/command role.

name/task_uuid/request_id are only used as: name -> a Blender object rename (obj.name = name), and task_uuid/request_id -> parameters to Hyper3D's own download/status API (hyperhuman.deemos.com or fal.run) using the caller's own API key; the actual GLB URL downloaded comes from that trusted API's own response, not the caller.

sink: requests.get(zip_file_url, stream=True) fetches any URL with an http/https scheme directly from the Blender addon process; the response is written to disk and imported as glTF (or, for the .zip/.obj fallback branch, extracted with a zip-slip check and imported as OBJ)
guard: partial: addon.py's import_generated_asset_hunyuan_ai only checks re.match(r'^https?://', zip_file_url) -- a bare scheme check. There is no allow-list restricting the host to Tencent's own result-file CDN, so the tool's own contract ('A model URL from ResultFile3Ds') is not actually enforced by code.
why: The tool description implies zip_file_url should be a URL returned by a prior Hunyuan3D generation job, but the implementation accepts any caller-supplied http(s) URL and fetches it server-side with no host allowlist and no exclusion of loopback/link-local/internal addresses -- classic SSRF surface reachable from a process that also holds Tencent Cloud credentials in memory. I could not confirm from static reading alone which internal endpoints would actually be reachable or what a real exploit would return (would require live network testing, which this audit forbids), so I am not claiming a proven exploit -- only a real mechanism with a plausible but unconfirmed impact, which is why this stays Tier B rather than A.
contract: zip_file_url: A model URL from ResultFile3Ds. Prefer a .glb URL when available; .zip/.obj URLs still work as a fallback.

why: job_id is only forwarded as a parameter to the addon's poll_hunyuan_job_status command, which reports Tencent Cloud job status using the caller's own credentials; no path/command/injection surface.

subscription_key/request_id are only forwarded to Hyper3D's own status API (hyperhuman.deemos.com POST body, or interpolated into a fal.run URL path segment) using the caller's own API key; worst case is calling a different endpoint on the same fixed, already-authorized third-party host.

feedback is validated against a fixed enum before use; correction_text/step_index/user_prompt are only placed as length-capped fields inside a structured JSON payload POSTed to Supabase via trajectory.py's _enqueue_row/_post_row -- no string concatenation into a command, path, or query, and no unstructured log line that could break parsing.

asset_type is validated against a fixed allowlist (['hdris','textures','models']) before being placed in the request; categories is passed through requests' own params= dict (properly URL-encoded), not string-concatenated into the URL.

category/licence are resolved through _polypizza_category_id/_polypizza_licence_id, which raise ValueError for anything outside the known name/id sets; the free-text query is percent-encoded with urllib.parse.quote before being placed in the URL path.

query/categories/count/downloadable are placed into requests' own params= dict for a GET to the fixed api.sketchfab.com/v3/search endpoint using the caller's own API key; requests handles encoding, no string-built URL or command.

object_name and texture_id are only used as lookup keys (bpy.data.objects.get, and a startswith() match over already-loaded bpy.data.images names); no file, command, or network sink is reachable from either argument.

sink: caller-supplied int flows unmodified from server.py build_deep_index -> IndexManagementService.rebuild_deep_index -> _execute_rebuild_workflow -> SQLiteIndexManager.refresh_index/build_index -> ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=...), which controls how many OS worker threads are spun up to process the indexed file set
guard: partial: index_management_service.py line 182 only rejects max_workers < 1; there is no upper bound anywhere in the chain
why: max_workers is directly caller-controlled via the tool's own schema and is passed unchanged into concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor with no ceiling. Actual thread creation is additionally bounded by the number of files ThreadPoolExecutor.submit() is called for (one submit per discovered file), so exploitability depends on set_project_path first being pointed at a project with a large file count; against a large/monorepo-sized or symlink-expanded tree this lets a caller force creation of very large numbers of OS threads with a single build_deep_index call, a genuine uncontrolled-resource-consumption issue rather than a crash-on-malformed-input case.
contract: max_workers: Maximum number of parallel workers for file processing. ... Increase for I/O-bound workloads on machines with many cores.

server.py:495 clear_settings(ctx) takes no data argument; SettingsService.clear_all_settings -> ProjectSettings.clear() only deletes two hardcoded filenames (config.json, legacy index.json) inside the server-computed settings_path, none of it caller-controlled.

code_intelligence_service.py analyze_file (line 35) calls self._require_valid_file_path -> ValidationHelper.validate_file_path (utils/validation.py:25), which rejects absolute paths and any '..'/'..\\' segment after normpath, then additionally verifies os.path.realpath(join(base_path, path)) starts with os.path.realpath(base_path) before the file is ever looked up, so traversal outside base_path is blocked twice.
server.py:512 get_file_watcher_status(ctx) takes no data argument; SystemManagementService.get_file_watcher_status only reads existing server-side state.
server.py:474 get_settings_info(ctx) takes no data argument; SettingsService.get_settings_info only reports the server's own settings/temp paths and config, none of it caller-supplied.

code_intelligence_service.py get_symbol_body (line 105) skips the explicit _require_valid_file_path check and joins base_path+file_path directly at line 182 (os.path.join(self.base_path, file_path)) before open(), which looks like a traversal gap; however the open() is only reached if index_manager.get_file_summary(file_path) (sqlite_index_manager.py:233) first returns a row, and that is an exact-match SQL lookup keyed on paths that were computed exclusively as os.path.relpath(abs_path, project_path) while walking project_path during indexing (sqlite_index_builder.py/json_index_builder.py), so a '..'-containing or absolute file_path can never match an existing row and the open() with the unsanitized path is unreachable in normal operation.

server.py:502 refresh_search_tools(ctx) takes no data argument; SearchService.refresh_search_tools only re-probes shutil.which() for fixed tool names (rg/ug/ag/grep) on the existing PATH.

configFile is sent verbatim as config_yaml to CircleCI's own /compile-config-with-defaults endpoint (src/clients/circleci/configValidate.ts) and never parsed, executed, or written locally by this repo's code.

outputDir is validated with resolveSafeOutputDir/joinWithinDir/safeWriteFileSync (src/lib/file-output/safePaths.ts, used from src/lib/usage-api/getUsageApiData.ts) which canonicalizes symlinks, denies system dirs and hidden/node_modules segments, and opens with O_NOFOLLOW; the downloaded URLs come from CircleCI's own job-status response, not the caller.

the tool takes no outputDir/path parameter from the caller; when FILE_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY is set it is an operator env var, and per-file names come from a regex-sanitized test.name (src/tools/getFlakyTests/handler.ts generateSafeFilename) that strips anything but [A-Za-z0-9_-].

csvFilePath is resolved through resolveSafeInputFile (src/lib/file-output/safePaths.ts) before fs.readFileSync in src/lib/usage-api/findUnderusedResourceClasses.ts readAndParseCSV, which rejects paths outside cwd/home/tmp roots and hidden/system segments including /etc.

projectSlug/branch/URLs only drive CircleCI API calls (remote-api-wrapper); outputDir, if provided, goes through resolveSafeOutputDir + joinWithinDir + safeWriteFileSync in src/lib/pipeline-job-logs/getJobLogs.ts formatJobLogs, the same guarded path-write primitive used elsewhere.

projectSlug/projectURL/workspaceRoot+gitRemoteURL/branch/jobNumber/pipelineNumber are only used to build CircleCI API requests in src/lib/pipeline-job-tests/getJobTests.ts; there is no filesystem, shell, or eval sink in this tool at all.

src/tools/getLatestPipelineStatus/handler.ts and src/lib/latest-pipeline/getLatestPipelineWorkflows.ts only resolve a projectSlug/branch and call CircleCI's pipeline/workflow APIs; no local sink of any kind.
src/tools/listArtifacts/handler.ts uses projectSlug/branch/URLs solely to call circleci.jobs.getJobArtifacts and formats the returned artifact URLs as text; the URLs are never fetched by this tool.

projectSlug/projectID/orgID/componentID/environmentID in src/tools/listComponentVersions/handler.ts are forwarded as path/query segments to CircleCI's own /deploy/* endpoints (src/clients/circleci/deploys.ts) on a fixed host; no local file, command, or eval sink exists.

the tool takes no input parameters at all (src/tools/listFollowedProjects/handler.ts / inputSchema.ts) and simply calls circleciPrivate.me.getFollowedProjects(); there is no caller-controlled data of any kind.

workflowId/workflowURL/fromFailed in src/tools/rerunWorkflow/handler.ts only select which workflow CircleCI's own rerun API acts on, scoped to whatever the caller's CIRCLECI_TOKEN can access; no local sink.

configContent and projectSlug/branch in src/tools/runPipeline/handler.ts are forwarded as the config.content field of CircleCI's own /project/:slug/pipeline/run API call (src/clients/circleci/pipelines.ts runPipeline); the config is compiled/executed by CircleCI's backend on the caller's own project, not by this process.

projectSlug/projectID/environmentName/componentName/currentVersion/targetVersion/namespace/reason/parameters in src/tools/runRollbackPipeline/handler.ts are packaged into a JSON body posted to CircleCI's own /projects/:id/rollback endpoint (src/clients/circleci/deploys.ts); the action executes against the caller's own CircleCI account/project, not locally.

src/tools/configHelper/handler.ts passes the caller's configFile string only as the `config` field of a JSON POST to CircleCI's own config-validate API (src/clients/circleci/configValidate.ts); it is never parsed, executed, templated, or written to disk locally, so there is no local sink for the argument.

outputDir flows through resolveSafeOutputDir/joinWithinDir/safeWriteFileSync in src/lib/usage-api/getUsageApiData.ts and src/lib/file-output/safePaths.ts, which canonicalizes symlinks with realpathBestEffort, blocks system directories and hidden/node_modules/launch-agent path segments, restricts writes to cwd/home/tmp (or an operator-set MCP_FILE_OUTPUT_ROOTS), and opens the destination file with O_NOFOLLOW to defeat a symlink-swap race; the only fetch() call in this path targets download_urls returned by CircleCI's own usage-export job-status response, not a caller-supplied URL.

projectSlug/projectURL/workspaceRoot+gitRemoteURL in src/tools/getFlakyTests/handler.ts only select which CircleCI insights/tests API endpoints are queried; the optional local file-write branch (writeTestsToFiles) writes under a directory built solely from the server-configured FILE_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY env var (never caller input) using filenames produced by generateSafeFilename, which strips test.name to [A-Za-z0-9_-] before use, so no caller-controlled path reaches fs.writeFileSync.

src/lib/usage-api/findUnderusedResourceClasses.ts readAndParseCSV calls resolveSafeInputFile(csvFilePath) (src/lib/file-output/safePaths.ts) before fs.readFileSync, which resolves symlinks and rejects any path outside cwd/home/tmp or landing on a system directory / hidden / node_modules segment, so a caller cannot read /etc/passwd, ~/.ssh, or similar outside the allowed roots.

formatJobLogs in src/lib/pipeline-job-logs/getJobLogs.ts validates outputDir with the same resolveSafeOutputDir + joinWithinDir + safeWriteFileSync(O_NOFOLLOW) guard used by download_usage_api_data before writing the log file; projectSlug/branch/projectURL/workspaceRoot+gitRemoteURL are only used to select CircleCI API calls via project-detection/index.ts, which does pure string parsing (no shell, no fs access).

src/tools/getJobTestResults/handler.ts forwards projectSlug/branch/jobNumber/pipelineNumber (derived via pure string parsing in project-detection/index.ts) to circleci.tests.getJobTests, i.e. CircleCI's own test-metadata API scoped to the caller's own token; there is no local file, shell, or eval sink.

src/tools/getLatestPipelineStatus/handler.ts only uses projectSlug/branch/projectURL/workspaceRoot+gitRemoteURL to look up pipeline status through CircleCI's own API (getLatestPipelineWorkflows); no local sink exists for any of the arguments.

src/tools/listArtifacts/handler.ts uses projectSlug/branch/projectURL/workspaceRoot+gitRemoteURL only to call CircleCI's pipelines/workflows/jobs APIs and list job artifacts; artifact URLs returned by CircleCI are echoed back as text, never fetched or written locally by this tool.

src/tools/listComponentVersions/handler.ts forwards projectSlug/projectID/orgID/componentID/environmentID verbatim to CircleCI's own deploys API (fetchEnvironments/fetchProjectComponents/fetchComponentVersions); results are only ever formatted into text, with no local file/shell/eval sink.

src/tools/listFollowedProjects/inputSchema.ts declares `z.object({})` — the tool accepts no caller-controlled arguments at all; the handler just calls circleciPrivate.me.getFollowedProjects() and formats the response.

src/tools/rerunWorkflow/handler.ts uses workflowId/workflowURL (workflowURL parsed by pure-string getWorkflowIdFromURL) only to select which workflow circleci.workflows.rerunWorkflow reruns via the caller's own CircleCI token; no local sink is reached.

nodes/connections are structurally validated (src/utils/validation.ts) and sent as the JSON body of POST /workflows (n8nApiWrapper.ts:110-132) to the caller's own n8n instance; any dynamic-code semantics of node types (e.g. a Code node) are enforced by the remote n8n engine, outside this repo's code.

param: none (unconditional -- fires on every list_workflows call regardless of the arguments supplied)
sink: console.error/stderr, dumping the axios instance's default headers object, which contains the literal X-N8N-API-KEY credential configured in environmentManager.ts's axios.create() (n8nApiWrapper.ts:57-62)
why: n8nApiWrapper.listWorkflows() (n8nApiWrapper.ts:246-258) has three console.error debug prints. Unlike every other debug line in this codebase -- e.g. environmentManager.ts:51-55 explicitly gates its own API-key log line behind `if (process.env.DEBUG === 'true')` -- these three lines are unconditional, so `console.error('[DEBUG] Headers:', api.defaults.headers)` writes the live n8n API key to stderr on every single list_workflows call, in every deployment, not just when DEBUG=true. This is a real secret-in-log exposure (CWE-532/CWE-200), but the leak does not hinge on any caller-supplied argument value -- calling the tool at all with any arguments (even {}) triggers it -- so it fails Tier-A criterion 1 (argument-driven) even though the mechanism itself is unambiguous and unguarded; filing as Tier B.

All string params (name, note, projectId/Name, parentTaskId/Name, tags) are run through escapeAppleScriptString before interpolation into the generated AppleScript in src/tools/primitives/addOmniFocusTask.ts; dueDate/deferDate/plannedDate only ever splice numeric Date components (via createDateOutsideTellBlock) and estimatedMinutes/repeat are validated as number/enum by zod, so no caller string reaches the script unescaped.

Same pattern as addOmniFocusTask: name/note/folderName/tags go through escapeAppleScriptString or escapeForJsonInAppleScript, dates go through the numeric-only createDateOutsideTellBlock, and repeat is compiled through repetitionRule.ts's whitelisted enums/integers.

batchAddItems.ts (primitive) is a pure orchestration wrapper that forwards each item's fields verbatim to addOmniFocusTask/addProject, which independently escape every string field; no additional AppleScript/JXA is generated in this file itself.
batchRemoveItems.ts just loops over items and calls the already-guarded removeItem() for each; it introduces no script generation or new sink of its own.

name, parentTagID and parentTagName are all passed through escapeAppleScriptString (and escapeForJsonInAppleScript for the JSON error payload) before being spliced into the generated AppleScript in createTag.ts.
dumpDatabase() takes no parameters at all (its MCP schema declares none); it only runs the fixed @omnifocusDump.js script, so there is no caller-controlled input to trace.

id/name/newName/newNote/tag lists and project/folder path lookups all go through escapeAppleScriptString or escapeForJsonInAppleScript in editItem.ts; date fields go through generateDateAssignmentV2 -> createDateOutsideTellBlock, which only ever emits numeric Date components; enum fields (newStatus, newProjectStatus) are validated by zod and mapped to fixed literals in code, and newRepeat goes through repetitionRule.ts's whitelisted compiler.

sink: spliced unescaped (except backslash/backtick/$) into a double-quoted JS string literal inside the `const argv = [...]` array that is embedded in the JXA wrapper script and executed via `app.evaluateJavascript()` inside osascript
guard: bypassable: escapeContent() (src/utils/scriptExecution.ts:335-340) only escapes backslash, backtick and $ -- it never escapes a literal double-quote or newline, even though the value is placed inside a double-quoted JS string. A perspectiveName such as `x", (function(){ ATTACKER_CODE(); })()); //` closes the string early and runs an arbitrary trailing IIFE as part of the OmniJS script OmniFocus evaluates.
why: perspectiveName is caller-controlled per its own zod schema (z.string(), no restriction, see src/tools/definitions/getPerspectiveView.ts:6). I traced it from the handler through getPerspectiveView() into executeOmniFocusScript(scriptPath, [perspectiveName, limit.toString()]) in scriptExecution.ts, where args are quoted with escapeContent and joined into `const argv = [...]`. Unlike queryOmnifocus.ts's escapeJXA (which does escape quotes), escapeContent does not, so a perspectiveName containing a double quote breaks out of the string and injects arbitrary OmniJS that runs inside OmniFocus's automation engine with the same privileges as the rest of the script -- turning a nominally read-only 'get this perspective' tool into arbitrary code execution against the whole database (create/delete/modify any task or project, and Omni Automation's networking APIs such as URL.fetch could exfiltrate data), which is a genuine confidentiality/integrity violation beyond the tool's declared contract.
contract: Get the items visible in a named OmniFocus perspective

sink: spliced verbatim (zero escaping) as a raw JS property-access expression inside the generated JXA sort comparator (generateSortLogic), which is written to a temp file and executed via osascript -l JavaScript
why: sortBy is caller-controlled per its own zod schema (z.string().optional(), no enum -- src/tools/definitions/queryOmnifocus.ts:46), described only informally as accepting field names like 'name, dueDate, ...' but nothing in code enforces that. Every other filter value in this same file (projectName, taskName, tags, status, etc.) is passed through the file's own escapeJXA() helper before interpolation, but generateSortLogic() (line 671-694) interpolates sortBy directly into `a.${sortBy}`/`b.${sortBy}` with no quoting and no escaping at all -- it is not even inside a string literal, so no quote-escaping would be needed to defend it; any value works as raw code. A sortBy of `x = (function(){ /* attacker OmniJS runs here */ return 0; })()` produces `let aVal = a.x = (function(){ ... })();`, which is syntactically valid and executes the attacker's IIFE with full access to the OmniFocus document model on every element compared during Array.prototype.sort -- turning the declared read-only query tool into arbitrary code execution (can create/delete/modify any task or project, and Omni Automation networking APIs could exfiltrate data). The `fields` array (z.array(z.string())) has an independent, equally unescaped fallback sink at generateFieldMapping() line 850 (`${field}: item.${field} !== undefined ? item.${field} : null`) for the same root cause -- no escapeJXA applied -- though it is harder to craft a single clean field value across all three raw substitutions there, so sortBy is the clearer, directly provable bypass.

sink: componentName is interpolated verbatim, with no regex-metacharacter escaping, into a RegExp pattern that is then run via .match() against the full text of the registry-ui.ts (or _registry.ts) file fetched from GitHub

A value containing a classic catastrophic-backtracking sub-pattern (nested/overlapping quantifiers) makes the resulting regex exhibit exponential-time backtracking against the multi-KB registry file content, tying up the Node event loop -- a targeted availability mechanism (ReDoS), not a generic malformed-input crash. This was reasoned statically from the code per the task's no-execute rule; I did not actually run the server to time the hang.

why: handleGetDirectoryStructure (src/tools/repository/get-directory-structure.ts:5-25) passes owner/repo/path/branch straight through to axios.buildDirectoryTree with only '|| default' fallbacks, never enforcing that owner/repo stay pinned to shadcn-ui/ui as the tool's description implies. A caller can therefore point this tool at any owner/repo/branch/path on api.github.com. If the deployer set GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN (optional, for higher rate limits), that credential is silently reused for the caller-chosen repo, letting the tool be used to browse repos the token can see beyond shadcn-ui/ui. I could not confirm from static code whether a given deployment actually has that token configured, which is why this is Tier B rather than A.

sink: assertSqlOperationAllowed() classifies the query only by its leading keyword; the sql is then run via executeQuery()/db.query() once per iteration (iterations is caller-controlled with no schema max)
guard: bypassable: sql="EXECUTE PROCEDURE <writing-procedure>" — assertSqlOperationAllowed() and checkAllowedOperation('EXECUTE') always allow the EXECUTE keyword by default, so a stored procedure that performs INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL internally runs (repeatedly, `iterations` times) without ALLOW_RAW_SQL=true
why: This tool exists to benchmark a query by executing it multiple times, and it reuses the same assertSqlOperationAllowed()/checkAllowedOperation() gate as execute-query. Because that gate only inspects the SQL's leading keyword, EXECUTE PROCEDURE calls are always permitted and can trigger arbitrary writes inside the called procedure, repeated `iterations` times (no upper bound in the Zod schema). Exploitability depends on a writable stored procedure already existing in the target database, which this static review cannot confirm.
contract: SQL operation ${normalizedOperation} is disabled by default. Set ALLOW_RAW_SQL=true to enable trusted raw writes.

sink: each query.sql in the caller-supplied batch (up to 20 queries, 10-way concurrency) is checked with assertSqlOperationAllowed() then executed via executeBatchQueries()->executeQuery()->db.query()
guard: bypassable: queries=[{sql:"EXECUTE PROCEDURE <writing-procedure>"}] — identical bypass to execute-query, applied independently to every item in the batch
why: Same root cause as execute-query: assertSqlOperationAllowed() treats EXECUTE as always-permitted regardless of what the called procedure does internally, so a batch entry can invoke a stored procedure that performs writes/DDL without ALLOW_RAW_SQL=true. This requires a writable procedure to already exist in the target database, which cannot be confirmed statically.
contract: SQL operation ${normalizedOperation} is disabled by default. Set ALLOW_RAW_SQL=true to enable trusted raw writes.

sink: assertSqlOperationAllowed(sql) classifies the query only by its leading keyword via getSqlOperation(); when that keyword is EXECUTE, checkAllowedOperation('EXECUTE') is checked against the default allowedOperations=['SELECT','EXECUTE'] and always passes, then executeQuery()->db.query() runs it
guard: bypassable: sql="EXECUTE PROCEDURE <writing-procedure>" — the write-protection gate (which requires ALLOW_RAW_SQL=true for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP/etc.) only inspects the SQL's leading keyword, so wrapping a write inside any stored procedure and invoking it via EXECUTE PROCEDURE sails through the gate untouched
why: execute-query accepts a fully caller-controlled sql string. Once assertSqlOperationAllowed() and checkAllowedOperation() pass, it is sent verbatim to the Firebird driver. Both checks treat the literal keyword EXECUTE as always-allowed by default, so calling any stored procedure that itself performs writes/DDL bypasses the tool's own stated write-protection ('disabled by default, set ALLOW_RAW_SQL=true'). Whether this is exploitable in a given deployment depends on a writable stored procedure already existing in that Firebird database, which this static review cannot confirm — hence Tier B rather than A.
contract: SQL operation ${normalizedOperation} is disabled by default. Set ALLOW_RAW_SQL=true to enable trusted raw writes.

sink: channel.createWebhook({avatar}) -> discord.js GuildChannelManager.createWebhook() -> DataResolver.resolveImage(avatar) -> resolveFile(): any string starting with 'http(s)://' is fetch()'ed server-side, and any other non-'data:' string is treated as a local filesystem path and read with fs.readFile()
dep_evidence: node_modules/discord.js@14.26.5 src/util/DataResolver.js lines 83-106 (resolveFile) and src/managers/GuildChannelManager.js line 234 (resolvedImage = await resolveImage(avatar)) — resolveImage/resolveFile apply no scheme or host allow-list before fetching or reading from disk; the library's own JSDoc for BufferResolvable warns 'discord.js will fetch the URL internally in order to create a Buffer. This can pose a security risk when the URL has not been sanitized'
why: The `avatar` argument (a bare z.string(), no format restriction) flows unchanged from the MCP tool args into discord.js's createWebhook call, which resolves it via resolveImage->resolveFile. A URL such as an internal cloud-metadata address is fetched by the MCP server process itself (SSRF), and any value that is not an http(s) URL or a data: URI is instead resolved with path.resolve() and read from the local filesystem via fs.readFile, uploading that file's bytes to Discord as the webhook avatar — an arbitrary local file read/exfiltration primitive. Neither the schema nor the handler validates or restricts the value at all.

guard: partial: only millisecond Date.now() entropy, no os.tmpdir() indirection, no O_EXCL/exclusive-create flag and no restrictive file mode; a locally co-resident attacker who pre-creates a symlink at the predictable /tmp/values-<ms>.yaml path before the call is made can redirect the write to an arbitrary path the server process can write to (same pattern repeats in the useTemplate code path at lines 269-271 for /tmp/values-*.yaml and /tmp/helm-template-*.yaml)
why: Every install with an inline `values` object (or useTemplate mode) writes attacker-supplied YAML through a predictably-named temp file in a shared world-writable directory with no exclusive-create/O_EXCL and no restrictive mode, which is the classic TOCTOU symlink-race pattern for insecure temp files (CWE-377); exploitability requires a second local actor able to pre-plant a symlink at the guessed path, which I cannot confirm is present in a given deployment.

the 'set' operation only ever runs `kubectl config use-context <contextName>` where contextName is required to already appear in the output of `kubectl config get-contexts -o name` (checked just before use), so an attacker cannot inject an arbitrary flag-shaped or credential-redirecting value as the context name.

why: This tool is the only one of the temp-file writers that added a restrictive mode, which meaningfully reduces confidentiality exposure of the resulting file's contents, but it does not close the underlying symlink pre-plant/TOCTOU path since no exclusive-create flag is used and the filename remains guessable; kept at Tier B given the partial mitigation and the local-attacker precondition.

This has no direct local-filesystem impact by itself, but it lets an attacker plant a traversal-shaped object name in a bucket that could later be paired with gnfd_download_object's unsanitized objectName-to-local-path join for a write outside the intended directory; on its own it only affects a remote/on-chain namespace so impact is not fully provable without chaining to another tool.
